conclusion: The stated Windows CPU/CUDA Q27/Q24 original consumers passed single-full-packed-M2 head and actual pending-to-embedding feedback; the focused CUDA descriptor bounds also passed.

implementation.qualification: Provider cold-caches its existing actual device Environment: current non-Orin NVIDIA MMVQ common domain M1..4, Orin M1. The default internal caller remains M1. No model/MTP whitelist, new user configuration or hot device query.
implementation.bounds: Canonical rank2 recognized GGUF logicalF32 RHS, denseF32 activation/output, K%512, retained signed logical/block/byte/stride limits; new M>1 also requires even N for two-row native reads. Other operand limits remain unchanged.
implementation.native: Admitted new batches reach fixed MMVQ before MMQ/cuBLAS; one original packed bank is reused, with bounded per-row Q8_1 activation scratch and no full F32 weight expansion. The proof is fixed-source and not an all-device native test.
implementation.consumers: Two actual M1 normalized-hidden leases are concatenated in an ordinary Graph. One full MatMul reads the original Q27Q6_K or Q24Q4_K head, stable TopK1 yields two separately owned row IDs, and a second ordinary Graph feeds both actual ID leases to the original full embedding. Original six-resource acceptance/continuation and old result leases remain checked.
implementation.reference: Each listed consumer checks all 2*248320 logits against original bytes and the existing independent actual-F32 activation-codec certificate. No new native reference batches, generated vocabulary or full F32 weight shadow.
implementation.builds: Four host TUs (two provider implementation TUs and two test TUs), one link, shared cached native inputs. The changed private tensor header is included in frozen compile dependencies. No SDK, CPU worker, NVCC or shader rebuild.

limitations: Native numeric coverage is the listed Windows CPU/CUDA Q27Q6_K and Q24Q4_K M2 workloads. Descriptor prepare M4 and fixed-source mapped-codec proof are not M4/all-codec/all-GPU numeric execution.
Orin large-packed M2 and larger batches needing MMQ qualification remain unsupported by this narrow admission. Two M1 calls do not close that gap.

Inputs are two actual M1 NextN normalized-hidden results; this does not establish two-token NextN or target equivalence. Actual target blocks/full verifier and finite external target hidden/history remain separate remaining work.
No prompt-to-output trained-model quality, natural acceptance rate, loading/TPS speedup or measured physical memory/VRAM result. Protected AV performance and the Q35 executable remain unchanged.
